PagerBot: PAGER — Streaming tail latency spike detected in eu-west2. p99 for /v1/stream/generate > 1500ms for 6m. Paging on-call: @alex.nguyen.

alex.nguyen: ack. Beginning triage. Is this isolated to streaming endpoints? Any error budget alerts firing?

maya.sre: looking. p95 and p99 both moved, but CPU/gpu on the serving hosts look nominal. Traces point to long socket connect/handshake times at the edge (router -> backend). Also seeing higher DNS resolution times to internal service discovery.

jorge.netops: infra telemetry: NAT gw in eu-west2c has ephemeral ports at 89% utilization, conntrack entries high. Also seeing spikes in ICMP fragmentation events between AZc <-> AZa.

alex.nguyen: ok immediate checklist: 1) surface affected customers 2) short-term mitigation to reduce port churn and cross-AZ egress 3) gather packet captures & DNS traces. @irene-cs, which customers are impacted?

irene-cs: CS reports three customers with active streaming sessions showing 503s and stalls; one customer opened a Sev ticket. I'll escalate and notify account owners.

sam-pm: did anything change in routing or NAT config today? I want to rule out recent pushes.

deploy-bot: LB config update 3091230000 -> edge-route-weighting (eu-west2) deployed 45m ago, rollout 100%. No rollbacks.

maya.sre: interesting — router logs show intermittent DNS timeouts to the service discovery endpoints which then fall back to IP; fallback causes new TCP connects to different AZs frequently. Sample log: 

```
2026-03-15T11:12:01Z router-euw2c WARN resolver timeout 200ms svc=mesh-sd-euw2 src=10.32.4.5
2026-03-15T11:12:01Z router-euw2c INFO fallback to A-record 10.64.2.18 chosen AZ=eu-west2a
2026-03-15T11:12:02Z router-euw2c WARN tls_connect ms=1320 dst=10.64.2.18:443 (retry)
```

jorge.netops: so two issues compounding: DNS flakiness causing cross-AZ connection shifts + NAT ephemeral exhaustion due to many short-lived connections. Mitigations we can do quick: 1) increase NAT capacity / add second NAT in eu-west2c, 2) enable DNS cache TTL overrides on routers to avoid aggressive fallbacks, 3) set stronger connection reuse (keepalive) in edge routing. Which can we do now?

alex.nguyen: prioritize 1 and 3. Jorge, can you spin up an extra nat-gw or a smaller instance that'll serve as SNAT? Maya, can you flip keepalive at router level? Prefer not to touch DNS TTLs unless necessary.

jorge.netops: provisioning a small NAT instance now (t3a.small) as failover and updating route tables to use it for SNAT. Should be live in ~7m.

maya.sre: flipping router keepalive to 60s for a 10% canary. Command in configMgmt: `router.edge.keepalive=60s`. Rolling 10% now.

irene-cs: customers asking for ETA. I'll give 15m and offer region fallback if they prefer.

[~8m later]

PagerBot: infra update — supplemental NAT instance provisioned at 3091234580 and added to SNAT pool.

jorge.netops: NAT added. Ephemeral port usage dropped from 89% -> 54% within 2 minutes. Conntrack entries trending down.

maya.sre: keepalive 10% canary good. No regressions in connection success. Rolling to 100% now.

alex.nguyen: monitoring p99 and streaming stall rate. Also start a short tcpdump for handshake analysis and DNS queries to capture root cause. Jorge, Maya, coordinate capture.

jorge.netops: running capture on router-euw2c for 5m for SYN/ACK and ICMP: 
```
sudo timeout 300 tcpdump -w /tmp/euw2c-handshake.pcap 'tcp[tcpflags] & (tcp-syn|tcp-fin) != 0 or icmp' 
```

maya.sre: exporting DNS resolver latencies and TLS handshake histogram for the last 30m to incident doc. Early glance: DNS latency spikes coincide with the worst p99 windows.

[~6m later]

maria.sre: (note: this is maya actually) p99 for /v1/stream/generate reduced from ~1600ms -> ~420ms after NAT add + keepalive rollout. Streaming stalls reduced ~70%.

irene-cs: customers updated. One customer still wants a mitigation timeline and asks for rate-limiting since their client spawns a new connection per utterance.

sam-pm: action items: short-term: auto-scale NATs at 80% ephemeral usage, enable router DNS cache override for critical discovery hosts, runtime: enable connection pooling and keepalive defaults for streaming SDKs. Mid-term: per-customer telemetry & throttles.

alex.nguyen: agreed. For immediate handoff: Maya will own post-incident analysis and attach pcaps + histograms. Jorge will own infra follow-ups (auto-scale NAT playbook). Irene will own CS comms. Sam to create backlog tasks for SDK/runtime changes. I'll hand off to next on-call in 10m.

maya.sre: captured pcaps and DNS traces. Preliminary note: many SYN bursts originate from a small subset of client IP blocks making many short-lived outbound streams. We'll include IPs in postmortem.

PagerBot: Incident marked mitigated at 3091234899 by added NAT capacity + routing keepalive. Channel remains open for postmortem and CS follow-up. :white_check_mark:

[thread ends]
